dedupe_keys.name: noaa national water model nwm wrf hydro based

description: The National Water Model (NWM) of NOAA's Office of Water Prediction is a hydrologic modelling framework that simulates observed and forecast streamflow over the continental United States, southern Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands. Its core is the NCAR-supported WRF-Hydro model with the Noah-MP land surface model, diffusive wave surface routing, subsurface routing on a 250 m grid and Muskingum-Cunge channel routing on the National Hydrography Dataset, with over 5,000 reservoirs and assimilation of USGS and USACE streamflow observations. Configurations run analyses and deterministic or ensemble forecasts from 18 hours to 30 days, producing streamflow for over 2.7 million river reaches and gridded land surface output; since version 3.0 it couples to the SCHISM coastal-estuary model for total water level guidance on the coasts. The model complements official river forecasts at about 4,000 points, and its outputs, flood inundation maps (covering nearly the whole country by September 2026) and hydrofabric shapefiles are free through the National Water Prediction Service; no licence is stated on the model page. Caveats: it is an operational national system, not a package users run locally, reach-scale guidance is not an official forecast, and performance varies in small, regulated or snow-dominated basins. Simulation uses: forecast flows and inundation for water infrastructure digital twins, flood exposure of treatment plants, dams and roads, reservoir operations, and coastal compound flooding. Related records: the USGS Water Data APIs (data-usgs-water-data-apis).
